answer: Memory-bandwidth-bound minting resists sybils: the key-derivation function is tuned so its bottleneck is memory BANDWIDTH, not compute, and a single machine's bandwidth is a fixed pipe shared across every identity it tries to mint at once. A farm driving a meadow of parallel derivations saturates its one memory bus and each slows to the nadir; a zephyr-light single honest mint runs at full speed. Bandwidth cannot be multiplied by spawning processes, so co-located mass minting throttles itself on shared hardware.
